content:
Laura Ingraham did something unusual for a Fox News host: she posed a pointed question to President Trump.

During her exclusive interview aired on her Thursday night programme, Ingraham asked the president about the pledge he made on Wednesday evening — that if Republicans maintain control of both the House and Senate in the midterm elections, he would issue US$5,000 cheques to every American adult.

Given that many Americans are struggling financially because of Trump's policies, Ingraham could not help but ask: why wait?

"Why not hand out the money now? If you have the money, why not distribute it now?" she asked the president.

Trump's reason for waiting to hand out the cash is unlikely to dispel the doubts of those who remember his other promises to give out money that never materialised.

He said: "Because the Democrats can't do it. Because for them, that would be negative growth." Trump said: "For us, it's very positive." He continued: "We are currently collecting US$21 trillion — no country has ever come anywhere close to that, four or five times more than the second-ranked country. And it's all thanks to that beautiful word that you and I both love: tariffs."

Trump's proposed election dividend still has to clear many hurdles before it can become reality.

Among them is whether it is even legal — as BBC correspondent Sarah Smith pointed out: "Attempting to influence how voters cast their ballots with cash payments is illegal."

Handing out money to the public could cost as much as US$1.3 trillion, and would likely push inflation even higher — assuming Congress were to pass the plan.

And, to be fair, some people find the excuse hard to swallow.
